short: Thailand has no AI law. ETDA and the digital ministry held a public hearing on the draft principles of an AI law from 11 to 24 June 2025; the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 binds, with administrative fines of up to 5 million baht.
title: Thailand AI Laws
subtitle: A draft AI law at the principles stage, and the PDPA that binds
body_html:
Status at a glance

Draft AI law, not yet before parliament. Thailand has no AI law. The Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA), with the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society, put the draft principles of an AI law ((ร่าง) หลักการของกฎหมายว่าด้วยปัญญาประดิษฐ์) to public hearing from 11 to 24 June 2025. The draft is risk-based, concentrates on high-risk uses, and would work through sector regulators, with provisions on sandboxes and text and data mining. The binding layer is the Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562 (2019). Verified on 25 October 2026 against ETDA and the Act's gazette text as the digital ministry publishes it.

Key instruments

InstrumentNumberPublishedIn force
Draft principles of an AI lawETDA public hearing draft11 June 2025; comments to 24 June 2025No
Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562Royal Gazette, vol. 136, part 69 Kor, 27 May 201927 May 2019In force

Who regulates and enforces

  • ETDA: drafted the AI law principles.
  • Office of the Personal Data Protection Committee: the PDPA, through its expert committee (s. 90).

Scope and reach

The PDPA applies to controllers and processors in Thailand, whether the processing happens inside or outside the Kingdom, and to foreign controllers and processors that offer goods or services to, or monitor the behaviour of, people in Thailand (s. 5); a foreign controller must appoint a representative in Thailand (s. 37(5)).

Core obligations

  • Today: the PDPA's duties, including the stricter rules on sensitive data (s. 26).
  • Under the draft, if enacted: duties for high-risk AI uses, set through the sector regulators.

Penalties

BreachMaximumProvisionEnforcer
Breaches involving sensitive data under s. 26An administrative fine of up to THB 5,000,000PDPA s. 84Expert committee
General breaches by a controllerAn administrative fine of up to THB 3,000,000PDPA s. 83Expert committee
Criminal offencesUp to 1 year's imprisonment, a fine of up to THB 1,000,000, or bothPDPA s. 79Courts

What is coming next

  • A draft AI bill following the 2025 hearing; a report of a further draft heard in July 2026 could not be confirmed on an official source.

Related

  • Global AI Laws: every jurisdiction compared, with the world map
  • AI Policy Ledger, the law tracker
  • AI lawsuit tracker and AI news

Sources

  • Draft principles of an AI law, public hearing, ETDA
  • Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562, gazette text, Ministry of Digital Economy and Society

Last verified

25 October 2026, against the sources above. Not confirmed on an official source and therefore left out: a reported July 2026 draft AI act with fines of 1 to 5 million baht, and a party bill on AI.
